newsitem.title: USA: Oneok, Western Resources to merge gas assets.
newsitem.headline: Oneok, Western Resources to merge gas assets.

text.p: Oneok Inc. and Western Resources Inc. said Thursday they agreed to an alliance combining the natural gas assets of both companies as part of a $660 million transaction.

Under the agreement, Tulsa-based Oneok, the parent of Oklahoma Natural Gas Co., will acquire all the natural gas assets of Western Resources, making it the ninth largest gas distribution company in the United States, serving 1.4 million customers.
Topeka, Kan.-based Western Resources, formerly Kansas Power & Light Co., has about 648,000 gas customers in Kansas and Oklahoma and also provides electricity to about 600,000 customers.
As part of the deal Western Resources will receive a combination of common and convertible preferred stock, making it the largest equity holder of Oneok.

Western Resources will receive about 3 million new shares of Oneok common stock and preferred stock that will be convertible, upon necessary regulatory approvals, into about another 19.3 million shares of Oneok common.
Oneok's stock was trading at $26.125, down 37.5 cents, at midday on the New York Stock Exchange. Western Resources' stock was up 50 cents at $31.125, also on the NYSE.
The agreement, approved by the boards of both firms, is expected to add to the earnings of both companies in the first year, they said.

"This strategic alliance allows us to market electricity, security and other unregulated services to a new set of customers -- Oneok's 735,000 customers," Western Resources Chairman John Hayes Jr. said in a statement.

"In addition, Western Resources will pursue its plan to market electricity, security and natural gas nationally. Under this plan, Oneok will procure natural gas for Western Resources' national marketing effort."

The companies said Oneok's independence would be preserved by standstill provisions in the agreement that define the rights and responsibilities of the respective companies for at least the next 15 years.

Western Resources will receive a preferred dividend of 1.5 times the underlying common dividend, which now stands at 30 cents a share, but no less than $1.80 per preferred share per year for the first five years.
The deal is expected to close by mid-1997, following approval by Oneok shareholders and federal and state regulatory authorities.
Oneok Chairman Larry Brummett said the transaction was part of his strategy to pursue strategic alliances or acquisition opportunities in natural gas distribution and energy-related businesses.
Additionally, it strengthens Oneok's balance sheet for future cash transactions, he said.
Hayes said the transaction would significantly strengthen Western Resources' annual cash flow.
